[[United States national basketball team|Team competition]]}} }} '''Loren Gerard Woods'''{{Cite web|title=Loren Woods Stats|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/woodslo01.html|access-date=2021-05-18|website=Basketball-Reference.com|language=en}} (born June 21, 1978) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He previously played six seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). ==High school and college career== Born in [[St. Louis, Missouri]], Woods attended high school at [[Cardinal Ritter College Prep High School|Cardinal Ritter College Prep]]. He started his college career at [[Wake Forest University]], where he was supposed to take over the [[Center (basketball)|center]] position once [[Tim Duncan]] left. However, he transferred to the [[University of Arizona]].{{citation needed|date=May 2021}} ==Professional career== Woods was selected by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] in the second round of the [[2001 NBA draft]]. After leaving the Timberwolves, Woods played for the [[Miami Heat]] and the [[Toronto Raptors]], where he appeared in 45 games during the [[2004–05 NBA season|2004–05 season]] and posted a career best 3.9 points per game. On 15 August 2006, he signed with the [[Sacramento Kings]] as a backup center,[https://www.espn.com/espn/wire?section=nba&id=2550619 Kings sign C Loren Woods.][http://www.nba.com/kings/news/Kings_Sign_Loren_Woods.html KINGS SIGN LOREN WOODS TO A CONTRACT.] but he was waived before the season began.[http://fantasybasketball.usatoday.com/content/news.asp?sport=NBA&line=69551 Fantasy basketball: Player notes.] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110717175139/http://fantasybasketball.usatoday.com/content/news.asp?sport=NBA&line=69551 |date=17 July 2011 }} Woods joined the Lithuanian giants [[BC Žalgiris|Žalgiris Kaunas]] in 2007.[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/33912/180 Loren Woods comes back to Zalgiris.] In June 2007, he joined the Turkish side [[Efes Pilsen SK|Efes Pilsen]]. He signed two 10-day contracts with the [[Houston Rockets]] on 21 March and 1 April 2008.[https://www.espn.com/espn/wire?section=nba&id=3324689 Rockets sign Woods to second 10-day contract.][http://www.chron.com/disp/story.mpl/sports/5635802.html Woods set to sign.] He was then waived by the Rockets on 14 July 2008.[http://www.chron.com/disp/story.mpl/sports/bk/bkn/5887748.html Rockets release backup center Woods, sign Greene.] he signed again with Žalgiris Kaunas on 16 July. His tenure with the Rockets ended up being his last time in the NBA, as his final game was Game 1 of the 2008 Western Conference First Round against the Utah Jazz on April 19, 2008. In his final game, Woods played for only one minute but was able to record 2 points and 1 rebound. Houston would go on to lose the series to Utah in 6 games. Woods joined [[CAI Zaragoza]] in 2009.{{Cite web |url=http://www.talkbasket.net/news/cai-zaragoza-tabs-loren-woods.html |title=Talkbasket.net Zaragoza grabs Woods. |access-date=9 March 2009
